name: ceyx-heif-stack
description: Consuming manifest for the product build's vcpkg-supplied third-party stack: the HEIF stack (libheif + libde265 + kvazaar + aom) plus libwebp. Round-2 began this as the OD-2 overlay-port spike; D5 makes it load-bearing for the product build.
$comment-dependencies: CORE = what every consuming platform needs. libwebp is core because native/cmake/encode.cmake links it on all desktop platforms. The HEIF stack sits behind the `heif` feature below, which is a DEFAULT feature -- so an unqualified `vcpkg install` against this manifest resolves exactly what it resolved before D5, and .github/workflows/port_spike.yml keeps working unchanged. A leg that needs libwebp alone (the Linux product build passes -DDNG_ENABLE_HEIF=OFF) adds --x-no-default-features and skips building aom/libheif/kvazaar entirely, rather than paying for a stack it then disables.

heif.description: The HEIF encode/decode stack: libheif with the kvazaar HEVC encoder and the aom AV1 codec, plus libde265 for decode. libde265 and aom already arrive as transitive dependencies of libheif; they are ALSO listed explicitly because D5 consumes them directly (libde265 via the LIBDE265_* pre-seeding, aom via AOM_*), and a direct consumer must be a direct dependency -- otherwise a future libheif feature change could silently drop them from the install plan.

de265.description: libde265 ALONE, without libheif/kvazaar/aom. This is what the macOS product legs install (D5 leg 2): they take libde265 from vcpkg but still build libheif itself from source via fetch_heif_deps.sh, because Spec §3.2 disqualifies every registry libheif (none offers a kvazaar HEVC-encoder feature at any version, only x265/GPL-2.0). Installing the full `heif` feature there would build a second, unused libheif and pay for aom+kvazaar twice. Selected with --x-no-default-features --x-feature=de265, so the default `heif` feature (and port_spike.yml's use of it) is untouched.

$comment-overrides: N30: nothing floats with the baseline. libwebp and aom are REGISTRY ports, so an explicit override is what pins them. libde265 is deliberately absent from this list: it is supplied by the overlay port native/vcpkg/ports/libde265 (a fork), and overlay ports bypass the versions database entirely -- a version constraint cannot be applied to them. Its 1.1.1 pin is the literal `version` field in that port's own vcpkg.json, which is a stronger pin than an override (it selects the exact source tarball by SHA-512 in portfile.cmake).
